canonical_name: libcorrect -- convolutional (Viterbi) and Reed-Solomon forward error correction in C (Brian Armstrong, Quiet Modem Project)
lineage: A portable SUCCESSOR/RIVAL to Phil Karn's libfec (in the vault as libfec-karn, BLOCKED by its 32-bit x86 assembly): the same two code families -- convolutional codes decoded by Viterbi, and Reed-Solomon over GF(2^8) -- reimplemented in plain C with SSE optional, plus a libfec-compatible shim. Its tests are the ADVERSARIAL PAIR: a noise/erasure injector corrupts codewords, the decoders must recover them. Deepens the ECC lineage: Rockliff RS (1991) -> Karn libfec (1990s-2000s) -> libcorrect (2016-).
version: github.com/quiet/libcorrect master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)

example.input: random messages corrupted by the test's noise model
example.output: bit-error and block-error counts: decode succeeds within the code's correction bound

upstream_docs: Viterbi, Error bounds for convolutional codes, IEEE IT 1967
Reed & Solomon, Polynomial Codes over Certain Finite Fields, 1960

human_capability_summary.built_to: carry data across a channel that flips or erases symbols, and recover the message exactly
human_capability_summary.pressure: noise, erasures, burst errors; portability pressure that killed the assembly-bound predecessor
human_capability_summary.success_means: every codeword corrupted within the design bound decodes to the original message; beyond the bound, failure is detected or reported

human_environmental_pressure: channel noise, symbol erasure, CPU/platform diversity
human_failure_condition: miscorrection: the decoder returns the wrong message with confidence
behavioral_entry_point: raise the injected error rate past the correction bound in the tests and watch decode failures appear

lineage_relations.note: portable C replacement for Karn's libfec; libfec-compatible shim
the Viterbi algorithm: decoding codes vs decoding HMM states
